    pub(crate) fn to_unrooted_(&self, store: &StoreOpaque) -> Result<crate::Unrooted<T>> {

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

For this and the non-owned Rooted version: does it make sense for callers to pass in an &mut Vec<_> that we push onto so they can reuse an allocation if they have one handy?

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

We intentionally do not implement Eq/PartialEq for Rooted because it isn't clear what the correct thing to do is: reference equality or Wasm semantics-level equality (which is only valid for eqref subtypes). Instead we have Rooted::ref_eq and also Rooted::rooted_eq. Also Rooted::ref_hash for hashing.

We should do the same for Unrooted.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

Let's maybe not include "weak" here, and just say "In exchange, ..." because otherwise we are potentially misleading people into thinking that this is a weak reference that remains valid as the referent is alive (regardless whether we have GC'd since the reference was taken, or relocated the object, etc...)

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

And then here I would skip the first sentence, and make the paragraph dedicated only to the idiom/convention of returning Unrooted references.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

I don't think we need to discuss the internals/implementation here either. I think it is fine to just say something like

In exchange, because Unrooted references are not recorded in the root set, they can be used in non-mut Store contexts and operations on them are very cheap.
